```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = TRUE)
```

```{r}
shift2nurses = read.csv("newshiftmedNurses.csv", header = TRUE) #read in files
shift2facilities = read.csv("newshiftmedFacilities.csv", header = TRUE)
shift2nursesfacilities = read.csv("newshiftmedNurses&Facilities.csv", header = TRUE)
shift2nursesmonthly = read.csv("newshiftmedNursesMonthly.csv", header = TRUE)

shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023))
shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024))
shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025))

shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023))
shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2024 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2024))
shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2025 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2025))
shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023))
shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024))
shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025))

shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023))
shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024))
shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 = as.numeric(gsub("\\$", "", shift2nursesfacilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025))

shift2nurses$worked = ifelse(shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2023 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2024 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0, TRUE, FALSE)

shift2nurses$claimed = ifelse(shift2nurses$total_shifts_claimed_2023 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_claimed_2024 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_claimed_2025 > 0, TRUE, FALSE)

shift2nurses$cancelratio = (shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2023 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2024 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025) / (shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2023 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2024 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025)
shift2nurses$cancelratio[is.infinite(shift2nurses$cancelratio)] = shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2023 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2024 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025
shift2nurses$cancelratio[shift2nurses$cancelratio == 0 & (shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2023 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2024 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025 == 0)] = NA

shift2nurses$newshowrate2023 = shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2023 / (shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2023 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2023)

shift2nurses$newshowrate2024 = shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2024 / (shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2024 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2024)

shift2nurses$newshowrate2025 = shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2025 / (shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2025 + shift2nurses$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025)

shift2nurses_workers = shift2nurses[shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2023 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2024 + shift2nurses$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0, ]


```
```{r}
library(patchwork)
```

Objective: analyze money and make a facility model (?)
```{r}
summary(shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023)
summary(shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2024)
summary(shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023)
summary(shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025)
#summary(shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2024)
#summary(shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2025)
```

Question for facility data: what is the difference between posted wage and worked wage?

```{r}
ggplot(shift2nurses, aes(x = avg_wage_shifts_worked_2023)) + geom_boxplot() + ggplot(shift2facilities, aes(x = avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023)) + geom_boxplot()
```
nurses stats are way higher than the wages the facilities are posting, but there are many high outliers for the facility wage. are nurses simply going to these outliers?

```{r}
moneyfacilities = shift2facilities[shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023 > 37.45, ]
nomoneyfacilities = shift2facilities[shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2023 <= 37.45, ]

shift2facilities$wowmoney = shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2025 > 56.59
```

```{r}
summary(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025 / moneyfacilities$total_shifts_posted_2025)
summary(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025/ nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_posted_2025)
```
on average, facilities giving a high wage did get more shifts. they also had a higher proportion of workers given how much shifts they posted (on average, facilities offering a higher wage get almost 4 times the amount of the shifts)

additional research: the average hourly wage for an RN nurse is \$38 to \$45. So most facilities hire shiftmed nurses BELOW the wage they should be getting

```{r}
ggplot(shift2facilities[!is.na(shift2facilities$wowmoney), ], aes(x = total_shifts_worked_2025, fill = wowmoney)) + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "dodge", bins = 25) 
```

```{r}
sum(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)
sum(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE) / 3 
```


```{r}
summary(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_claimed_2025)
summary(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_claimed_2025)
summary(moneyfacilities$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025)
summary(nomoneyfacilities$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025)
summary(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025)
summary(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025)
```
more people on average claimed shifts for the facilities offering a higher wage (75th percentile is 120.8 vs. 6.75, huge jump). For cancels, facilities offering more money seemed to have less on average, but the IQR seems to be much higher. Is this due to the lack of claimed shifts for nomoneyfacilities? Do nomoneyfacilities just have extreme outliers? A strange interpretation: facilities offering a higher wage have half as many facility cancelled shifts as facilities offering a wage below the marker on average, but the IQR for facilities with a higher wage is a lot higher than the others. 

```{r}
value1 = mean(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)
value2 = mean(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)

temp2 <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Yes", "No"),  # x-axis labels
  Value = c(value1, value2)                 # y-axis values
)

ggplot(temp2, aes(x = Category, y = Value, fill = Category)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") + xlab("Is the Facility's Posted Wages Above the 75th Percentile?") + ylab("Mean Total Shifts Worked at Facility in 2025") + ggtitle("Facilities Posting a High Wage Look\n to Get More Worked Shifts on Average") + theme_light() + theme(text = element_text(size = 13), legend.position = "none") + geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 2), color = Category), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 6) + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,  150)) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgray", "#68119A")) +  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkgray", "#68119A"))
```
```{r}
value1 = mean(moneyfacilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025, na.rm = TRUE)
value2 = mean(nomoneyfacilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025, na.rm = TRUE)

temp3 <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Yes", "No"),  # x-axis labels
  Value = c(value1, value2)                 # y-axis values
)

ggplot(temp3, aes(x = Category, y = Value, fill = Category)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") + xlab("Is the Facility's Posted Wages Above the 75th Percentile?") + ylab("Mean Total Shifts Facility has Cancelled") + ggtitle("Facilities Posting a High Wage Have Half as Many\n Facility Cancels Compared to Facilities Who Do Not") + theme_light() + theme(text = element_text(size = 13), legend.position = "none") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,50)) + geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 2), color = Category), vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 6) + scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgrey", "#68119A")) +  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkgray", "#68119A"))
```


Question: are nurses fueled by money (does more average money earned = more shifts worked)?
```{r}
summary(shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025)

moneynurses = shift2nurses[shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 > 56.59, ]

nomoneynurses = shift2nurses[shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 <= 56.59, ]

shift2nurses$wmoney = shift2nurses$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 > 56.59

shift2nurses_workers$wmoney = shift2nurses_workers$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025 > 56.59
```

```{r}
summary(moneynurses$total_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(nomoneynurses$total_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(moneynurses$total_confirmed_shifts_2025)
summary(nomoneynurses$total_confirmed_shifts_2025)
summary(moneynurses$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(nomoneynurses$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2025)
```

```{r}
ggplot(shift2nurses_workers[!is.na(shift2nurses_workers$wmoney), ], aes(x = total_shifts_worked_2025, fill = wmoney)) + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "dodge", bins = 20) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,50)) + labs(fill = "Does the Nurse Make\n Above the 75th Percentile?")
```

on average, those who had an average wage above $56.59 (75th percentile) worked more shifts than those who were paid less
```{r}
value1 = mean(moneynurses$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)
value2 = mean(nomoneynurses$total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)

temp <- data.frame(
  Category = c("Yes", "No"),  # x-axis labels
  Value = c(value1, value2)                 # y-axis values
)

ggplot(temp, aes(x = Category, y = Value, fill = Category)) + geom_bar(stat = "identity", color = "black") + xlab("Does the Nurse Make Above the 75th Percentile?") + ylab("Mean Total Shifts Worked in 2025") + ggtitle("Nurses Who Make More Money\n Seem to Work More on Average") + theme_light() + theme(text = element_text(size = 15), legend.position = "none") + scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0, 30)) + geom_text(aes(label = round(Value, 2), color = Category),  vjust = -0.5, fontface = "bold", size = 6) +  scale_fill_manual(values = c("darkgray", "#68119A")) +  scale_color_manual(values = c("darkgray", "#68119A"))
```


```{r}
ggplot(shift2nurses[!is.na(shift2nurses$wmoney), ], aes(x = total_shifts_claimed_2025, fill = wmoney)) + geom_histogram(aes(y = after_stat(density)), position = "dodge", bins = 25) + scale_x_continuous(limits = c(0,50)) 
```
similar story for claimed shifts

Facilities and a facility ranking system

```{r}
head(sort(table(shift2facilities$facility_msa), decreasing = TRUE))
tail(sort(table(shift2facilities$facility_msa), decreasing = TRUE))
```
currently most popular and least popular msas... will this go into affect their score on my model?

```{r}
length(unique(shift2facilities$facility_msa))
mycounts = table(shift2facilities$facility_msa)
sum(mycounts <= 2)
sum(mycounts <= 2) / length(unique(shift2facilities$facility_msa))
```

more than 1/3 of facility msas have less than or equal to 2 facilties in the area

the model:
```{r}
shift2facilities$facpoints2025 = 0.5 * shift2facilities$total_shifts_claimed_2025 + shift2facilities$total_confirmed_shifts_2025 + 0.75 * shift2facilities$total_shifts_worked_2025 + 2 * shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2025 + 2.5 * shift2facilities$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2025 + 2 * shift2facilities$total_bundle_shifts_worked_2025 - shift2facilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025

shift2facilities$facpoints2025 = ifelse(shift2facilities$total_shifts_worked_2025 == 0, 0, shift2facilities$facpoints2025)

shift2facilities$facpoints2024 = 0.5 * shift2facilities$total_shifts_claimed_2024 + shift2facilities$total_confirmed_shifts_2024 + 0.75 * shift2facilities$total_shifts_worked_2024 + 2 * shift2facilities$avg_wage_shifts_posted_2024 + 2.5 * shift2facilities$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2024 + 2 * shift2facilities$total_bundle_shifts_worked_2024 - shift2facilities$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2024

shift2facilities$facpoints2024 = ifelse(shift2facilities$total_shifts_worked_2024 == 0, 0, shift2facilities$facpoints2024)
```

```{r}
head(sort(shift2facilities$facpoints2025, decreasing = TRUE))
```

```{r}
points2025 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  summarize(total_value = sum(facpoints2025, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%

meanpoints2025 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  summarize(total_value = mean(facpoints2025, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value)) 

meanpointsovertwo2025 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  filter(n() > 2) %>%
  summarize(total_value = mean(facpoints2025, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value))


works2025 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  summarize(total_value = sum(total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value)) 

meanworks2025 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  filter(n() > 2) %>%
  summarize(total_value = mean(total_shifts_worked_2025, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value)) 

bestfacs2025 = shift2facilities[, c("facility_id","facility_msa","facpoints2025")] %>%  
  arrange(desc(facpoints2025)) 

meanpointsovertwo2024 = shift2facilities %>%
  group_by(facility_msa) %>%    # Group by the categorical variable
  filter(n() > 2) %>%
  summarize(total_value = mean(facpoints2024, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  arrange(desc(total_value))

top8facs <- bestfacs2025 %>%
  arrange(desc(facpoints2025)) %>%

meanpointsovertwo2025
meanpointsovertwo2024
bestfacs2025
top8facs
top8msas
```
For sum: Best fac msas according to my model mostly follows just how much shifts were worked there... I believe this model is pretty accurate, but would another model be more accurate?

Average is a whole different story...

Different interpretations:
points2025: St. Louis is the MSA with the most total points
meanpoints2025: Goldsboro is the MSA with the highest average points per facility
meanpointsovertwo2025: Johnstown is the MSA with the highest average points per facility and has > 2 facilities in the MSA

I believe meanpointsovertwo is the best measure of quality of msa

Observation: individual facilities in bustling cities / metropolitan msas (st louis, philly, detroit, harrisburg, etc.) have the highest points, but the msas with the highest total average are less popular areas (johnstown, lancaster, rochester, etc.). they are cities, but just not as big as ones like new york and philly

```{r}
            total_count = n(),
    prop_zero = zero_count / total_count) 

ggplot(popmsas_zeroprop, aes(y = prop_zero, x = facility_msa, fill = facility_msa)) + geom_col(color = "black") + theme_light() + theme(text = element_text(size = 11), legend.position = "none") + scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Pastel1") + xlab("Facility MSA") + ylab("Proportion of Facilities that had 0 Worked Shifts") + ggtitle("Almost all of Chicago's Facilities Didn't\n Have a Single Nurse Work There") + scale_y_continuous(labels = c("0%","25%","50%","75%","100%"))
```
almost all of chicagos facilities have had 0 nurses work there... even for st. louis, a successful msa, over 50% of its facilities have had 0 nurses

$$0.5\text{ (Shifts Claimed) + Confirmed Shifts + } 0.75\text{ (Shifts Worked) + } \\
2\text{ (Average Wage Posted) + } 2.5\text{ (Guaranteed Shifts Worked) + }\\ 2\text{ (Bundle Shifts Worked) - Facility Cancels}$$

```{r}
            total_count = n(),
    prop_zero = zero_count / total_count) 

ggplot(popmsas2_zeroprop, aes(y = prop_zero, x = facility_msa, fill = facility_msa)) + geom_col(color = "black") + theme_light()
```

some extra stuff

investigating the st louis facility 
```{r}
bestfac = shift2nursesfacilities[(shift2nursesfacilities$facility_id == "20343") | (shift2nursesfacilities$facility_id == "10832") | (shift2nursesfacilities$facility_id == "9435"), ]
notbestfac = shift2nursesfacilities[shift2nursesfacilities$facility_id != "20343", ]

summary(bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025)
summary(bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
of the nurses who have worked at least one shift at the goated facilities, they averaged around 8 shifts worked in 2025. across all facilities, of the nurses who have worked at least one shift there, they averaged around 2 shifts worked at that facility in 2025

```{r}
summary(bestfac$total_confirmed_shifts_2025[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$total_confirmed_shifts_2025[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
of the nurses who are working, it looks as though confirmed shifts are being used a lot. (many nurses have more confirmed shifts than worked shifts)

```{r}
summary(bestfac$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$avg_wage_shifts_worked_2025[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
wage worked is similar... st louis mostly posts a high wage but all facilities have nearly the same worked wage?

```{r}
summary(bestfac$total_bundle_shifts_worked_2025[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$total_bundle_shifts_worked_2025[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
some outliers... but on average bundle shifts may not be a super popping feature

```{r}
summary(bestfac$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2025[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$total_guaranteed_shifts_worked_2025[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
guaranteed shifts have gotten used a little bit at higher level facilities

```{r}
summary(bestfac$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025)
summary(notbestfac$total_shifts_fac_cancel_2025)
summary(bestfac$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025)
summary(notbestfac$total_hcp_cancelled_shifts_2025)
```
for all nurses, the facility cancel rate is similar between top ranked facs and the other facs.so higher wage facilities cancel less, but the higher ranked facilities dont have significant evidence of cancelling less. sameish story for nurse cancels

```{r}
summary(bestfac$claimed_shift_ytd[bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
summary(notbestfac$claimed_shift_ytd[notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0])
```
presense of outliers. but those that worked at top level facilities are showing better retention

```{r}
(sum((bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0) & (bestfac$claimed_shift_ytd > 0))) / sum((bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0))
(sum((notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0) & (notbestfac$claimed_shift_ytd > 0))) / sum((notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0))

(sum((bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2024 > 0) & (bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0))) / sum((bestfac$total_shifts_worked_2024 > 0))
(sum((notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2024 > 0) & (notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2025 > 0))) / sum((notbestfac$total_shifts_worked_2024 > 0))
```
confirms above. those that work at higher level facilities are more likely to come back for them in the next year.

interpretation: 53% of nurses who worked at high level facilities in 2024 worked at those same facilities in 2025

```{r}
facilitiesworked = shift2nursesmonthly[shift2nursesmonthly$total_facilities_worked > 0, ] %>%
  group_by(caregiver_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_per_level = mean(total_facilities_worked, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  summarise(mean_of_means = mean(mean_per_level))

facilitiesworked2 = shift2nursesmonthly[shift2nursesmonthly$total_facilities_worked > 0, ] %>%
  group_by(caregiver_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_per_level = median(total_facilities_worked, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  summarise(mean_of_means = median(mean_per_level))

facilitiesworked3 = shift2nursesmonthly[shift2nursesmonthly$total_facilities_worked > 0, ] %>%
  group_by(caregiver_id) %>%
  summarise(mean_per_level = median(total_facilities_worked, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
  summarise(mean_of_means = mean(mean_per_level))

facilitiesworked
facilitiesworked2
facilitiesworked3
```
on average, users worked at about 1.3 - 1.4 facilities per month. so nurses usually only go to 1 facility
